extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for NIDCD K-series career development (K) awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing applications to NIDCD K-series career development awards (K01, K08, K18, K23, K24, K25, K43, K99/R00, etc.), including eligibility, required application components, institutional/mentor commitments, percent effort, duration, and budget caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit with NIDCD mission and strategic plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must demonstrate its contribution to NIDCD and its fit with NIDCD's mission, scientific program areas, and strategic plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This language is repeated for multiple K mechanisms; applicants should explicitly describe how the proposed research aligns with NIDCD priorities and current strategic plan. Cite relevant NIDCD scientific program areas when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional and mentor support statements (resources and contingency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should include statements from the institution and the mentor(s) addressing detailed information about who will provide the necessary resources; funding source and amount of additional funding (as needed); support staff available and committed to the project; availability of biostatistical support for the duration of the study, including the planning period; and a contingency plan (for the institution and mentor) for completion of the study in the event the awardee leaves the institution earlier than the end date of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly encouraged to provide clear evidence that adequate resources are available at the institution for the successful completion of the proposed research project. Each element (resource provider, additional funding, committed support staff, biostatistics, contingency plan) should be addressed explicitly in institutional/mentor letters or institutional statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select funding opportunity type by clinical trial allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH now provides three funding opportunities for most types of K awards: Independent Clinical Trial Not Allowed; Independent Clinical Trial Required; Basic Experimental Studies with Humans Required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must choose the FOA that matches the clinical trial status/requirements of the proposed work. See NIH comparison of funding opportunity types by clinical trial allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: K01 IRSDA eligibility and focus (International Research Scientist Development Award)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: provide support and protected time (three to five years) to advanced postdoctoral U.S. research scientists and recently appointed U.S. junior faculty (applicants must be at least two years beyond conferral of doctoral degree) for an intensive, mentored research career development experience in a low- or middle-income country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIDCD is especially interested in IRSDA applications focused on otitis media, hearing loss, early hearing detection and intervention (including newborn screening), chemosensory loss, health services, habilitation/rehabilitation services, dissemination & implementation research, and cultural/linguistic adaptations of diagnostic/intervention tools. Salary support up to $100,000/year; research support up to $40,000/year; duration 3–5 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: K01 Mentored Research Scientist Development Award (Parent K01) — purpose and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Used to support new and junior basic research investigators in supervised career development experiences that lead to research independence; also supports investigators who need protected time in supervised career development experiences to train in a new field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must demonstrate contribution to NIDCD and fit with its mission/program areas/strategic plan. Applicants are strongly encouraged to show evidence of adequate institutional resources (see institutional/mentor support statements). Salary support up to $75,000 plus fringe benefits/year; research support up to $30,000/year.

rubrics_metrics.name: K01 NIDCD Mentored Career Development Award for Postdoctorate Au.D./Ph.D. Audiologists — program requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports comprehensive and rigorous postdoctoral research training experiences for promising Au.D./Ph.D. audiologists; provides salary and research support for up to 3 years of protected time for intensive research career development under guidance of experienced mentors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must include an integrated program of research and training designed to enhance the individual's potential to develop into a productive independent researcher. Expectation that awardees will have a pathway to launch independent research careers and become competitive for R01-type funding. Salary up to $75,000/year; research support up to $30,000/year; duration up to 3 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: K08 Mentored Clinical Scientist Research Career Development Award — eligibility and effort requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports individuals with a clinical/health-professional doctorate interested in supervised career development experiences in basic clinical research (not patient-oriented research) that lead to research independence in biomedical, behavioral, or translational fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must demonstrate contribution to NIDCD and fit with mission/program/strategic plan; applicants should include institutional/mentor statements about resources. Salary support up to $100,000 plus fringe benefits/year. Non-surgeon scientists must devote a minimum of 75% full time professional effort to research and career development activities associated with the K award; surgeon-scientists must devote a minimum of 50% full time professional effort. Research support up to $50,000/year.

rubrics_metrics.name: K18 Research Career Enhancement Award for Established Investigators — eligibility and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Enables established, proven investigators to augment or redirect their research programs through acquisition of new research skills; provides 6 months to 2 years of advanced mentored research career development and requires a commitment of 25–50% professional effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible PD/PIs include doctoral-level investigators holding rank of associate professor or professor (or equivalent) with documented records of scientific accomplishments and research grant funding. NIDCD will contribute up to the legislative salary cap per year; research development support $40,000/year (must be justified and consistent with stage/proportion of time). Salary for mentors, secretarial/admin assistants not allowed. Indirect costs reimbursed at 8% of modified total direct costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: K23 Mentored Patient-Oriented Research Career Development Award — eligibility and effort requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports individuals with a clinical/health-professional doctorate in supervised career development experiences in research conducted with human subjects that lead to research independence in biomedical, behavioral, or translational fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must demonstrate contribution to NIDCD and fit with research priorities and strategic plan; include institutional/mentor statements about resources. Salary up to $100,000 plus fringe benefits/year. Non-surgeon-scientists must devote a minimum of 75% full time professional effort; surgeon-scientists must devote a minimum of 50% full time professional effort. Research support up to $50,000/year.

rubrics_metrics.name: K24 Midcareer Investigator Award in Patient-Oriented Research — applicant prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports well-established investigators interested in mentoring the next generation of investigators in NIDCD research areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must have active, peer-reviewed, independent research support from NIDCD at the time of submission; must have a mid-career faculty appointment at the associate professor level or higher; must be part of a Clinical and Translational Science Award (CTSA) that will provide resources to facilitate development of beginning clinical investigators. Salary support up to the maximum legislative salary cap for 25–50% effort; research support up to $50,000/year.

rubrics_metrics.name: K25 Mentored Quantitative Research Development Award — target audience and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports individuals with quantitative scientific and engineering backgrounds who have not had sustained involvement in biomedical/behavioral research and who wish to focus their research in areas supported by NIDCD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must demonstrate contribution to NIDCD and fit with mission/program areas/strategic plan; applicants should provide institutional/mentor statements about resources (see institutional/mentor support). Salary support up to $80,000 plus fringe benefits/year; research support up to $30,000/year.

rubrics_metrics.name: K43 Emerging Global Leader Award (Fogarty) — eligibility and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides research support and protected time (three to five years) to a low- or middle-income country (LMIC) early career research scientist who holds a junior faculty position at an LMIC academic or research institution, with the goal of leading to an independently funded research career at the LMIC institution or another LMIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIDCD is especially interested in proposals on topics within its mission (otitis media, hearing loss, early hearing detection and intervention, chemosensory loss, health services, habilitation/rehabilitation, dissemination & implementation, cultural/linguistic adaptations). Applications from institutions within a geographic region that share the same spoken language could offer special opportunities for regional collaboration. Salary up to $100,000/year; research development support up to $40,000/year; duration 3–5 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99/R00 Pathway to Independence Award — purpose and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Used to support outstanding senior postdoctoral investigators in NIDCD research areas who are ready to complete their transition to become independent investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must demonstrate contribution to NIDCD and fit with mission/scientific program areas/current strategic plan. Applicants are strongly encouraged to provide evidence of adequate institutional resources and include statements from the institution and mentor(s) (detailed resources, funding sources, support staff, biostatistical support, contingency plan). Salary up to $75,000 plus fringe benefits/year; research support up to $25,000/year.
